newsitem.title: USA: Flagstar snr noteholders await negotiation.
newsitem.headline: Flagstar snr noteholders await negotiation.

text.p: Senior noteholders of Flagstar Cos Inc are expected to begin negotiations over a restructuring plan that would reduce their coupons and extend debt maturities, a noteholders' lawyer said on Tuesday.
Daniel Golden of Stroock & Stroock & Lavan said senior noteholders are considering the restructuring plan that was outlined by Flagstar in a Securities and Exchange Commission S-4 filing on Monday.
Under the plan, holders of the 10-3/4 percent and 10-7/8 percent senior notes would receive a pro rata share of a new 9-3/4 percent senior note issue due 2007.
The maturities of the outstanding notes would be extended from 2001 and 2002, respectively, Golden said.

The new class of senior notes would have a principal amount of $575.9 million -- equal to the principal of the two original note issues plus accrued interest through an assumed effective date of the plan of October 1, 1997.
Senior noteholders would also receive a small cash payment, according to Barbara Wedelstaedt, an analyst with KDP Investment Advisors.
The plan is contingent upon receiving the consent of holders of the company's senior notes, Flagstar said.

Earlier this month, Flagstar said it reached a tentative agreement with holders of $847 million senior subordinated debt that would give those creditors 95.5 percent of stock of the restructured company.

The plan also provides for holders of Flagstar's convertible junior debentures to receive a 3.25 percent stake in the new company and holders of the company's cumulative convertible exchangeable preferred stock to receive 1.25 percent.
Existing common stockholders will receive five-year, out-of-the-money warrants to purchase seven percent of the fully diluted common stock in the new company.

Flagstar, based in Spartanburg, South Carolina, is one of the nation's largest restaurant companies. At the time of the tentative agreement, the company also stated it would not make a $7.1 million interest payment on its 11-3/8 percent senior subordinated debentures.
